newsitem.title: INDIA: Australia keen to invest in Indian ventures.
newsitem.headline: Australia keen to invest in Indian ventures.

text.p: Australia is keen to invest in joint ventures in India's mining, transport, agriculture and food processing sectors, an Indian government statement said on Tuesday.
The statement also quoted Australia's visiting deputy prime minister, Tim Fisher, as saying his country was keen to expand technological cooperation with India.
Fisher was quoted as telling Indian Industry Minister Murasoli Maran that India, through joint ventures, could gain from Australia's mining technology.
Another government statement said Indian Mining Minister Birendra Prasad Baishya welcomed the interest of Australian companies in minerals exploration in India.

"The interest shown by foreign investors to the economic reforms and the response of foreign mining giants, particularly the Australian companies, have been most enthusiastic," Baishya told a joint business meeting on mining.
Baishya said of the 24 foreign investment proposals cleared by India in recent months in the mining sector, about half related to Australian companies.
"I expect that the Australian mining corporates will play the most important role in the further development of Indian mining industry," he said.
